name: Mark a claim and an example
description: Mark which sentence states the claim and which sentence is only an example.
l1c: Underline the sentence that says what the piece wants you to accept.
l2c: Mark a different sentence as an example and write what it is an example of.
l2d: You can separate an example from the claim.
l3c: Give the marked page to someone else and ask them to point to the claim.
l3d: Someone else can use your marks.
safety: Do not invent a source for the claim.

name: Name who is quoted
description: Name the person whose words appear as a quote and the person who wrote the surrounding text.
l1c: Point to the quoted words and to the name attached to them.
l2c: Write the name of the person quoted and the name of the person who wrote the piece, or note which one is missing.
l2d: You can tell a speaker from a writer.
l3c: Find the next place that quote is attributed, or write that you cannot find it.
l3d: You can stop when the trail ends.
safety: Do not present a guess as the speaker's name.

name: Separate an ad from the report
description: Point to the part of a page that is selling something and the part that is reporting.
l1c: Point to one phrase or picture that asks you to buy, book, or sign up.
l1d: You can see a sales pitch.
l2c: Point to one sentence that tells what happened, and keep it separate from the pitch.
l2d: You can separate the two jobs of the page.
l3c: Write one fact you would need before treating the page as a report.
safety: Do not treat a label such as sponsored as optional if it is printed.

name: Write a claim you can check
description: Write one sentence another person can check, and name where they would look.
l1c: Write one claim in a sentence that names what would count as true.
l1d: You can state a checkable claim.
l2c: Add the page, object, or person a checker should use, or write that you have no place yet.
l3c: Ask someone to say whether they could check it, and revise the sentence if they cannot.
l3d: You can make the claim usable.
safety: Do not invent a citation.

name: Find a number that changed
description: Find one number that differs between two versions of the same note.
l1c: Put two versions of one note side by side and mark the dates or labels.
l1d: You can set up a comparison.
l2c: Circle one number that differs and write both values.
l2d: You can catch a changed number.
l3c: Write whether you checked the rest, and do not claim a number you did not compare.
safety: Do not change either version while you compare them.

name: Name the audience of a poster
description: Say who a poster is speaking to, using the words and the place it hangs.
l1c: Point to the words that name or imply a reader.
l1d: You can see who is addressed.
l2c: Say how the place it hangs supports or limits that guess.
l3c: Write the audience as a guess if the poster does not name them.
l3d: You can keep a guess visible.
safety: Do not remove or cover the poster.

name: Tell a preview from a review
description: Say whether a short text is selling a future showing or responding to a work the writer saw.
l1c: Point to a word that places the work in the future or in the past.
l2c: Point to one detail that could only come from seeing it, or write that there is none.
l2d: You can test whether they saw it.
l3c: Label it preview or review, and write the clue you used.
l3d: You can name the kind of text.
safety: Do not grade the work itself.

name: Find which date is which
description: On one page, say which date is the event and which date is the publication.
l1c: Write every date you can see on the page.
l2c: Label one date as the event and one as the publication, or say the page does not show both.
l2d: You can give dates different jobs.
l3c: Say which date you would cite if you mentioned the event.
l3d: You can choose the date that matches the job.
safety: Do not invent a date that is not printed.

name: Mark a judging word
description: Mark one word that judges and one word that only describes.
l1c: Underline one word that says what is there.
l1d: You can find a describing word.
l2c: Underline one word that praises, blames, or ranks, and say so.
l2d: You can find a judging word.
l3c: Write the same sentence with the judging word replaced by a description.
safety: Do not shame the writer.

name: Name one absence
description: Name one fact, person, or group a short piece does not mention, and why that matters to the claim.
l1c: Write the claim in your own sentence.
l2c: Name one thing the piece would need to mention for you to follow the claim.
l3c: Say how that absence changes what you can conclude, in one sentence.
safety: Do not invent the missing fact.

name: Test a caption against the picture
description: Say one thing a caption claims that the picture shows, and one thing it does not show.
l1c: Write the caption's main claim in your words.
l2c: Point to the part of the picture that supports the claim, or write that you cannot find it.
l3c: Write one thing a viewer still cannot know from the picture alone.
safety: Do not name a private person who did not agree.

name: Save a clip with its page
description: Save a short clip or quote only together with the page or person it came from.
l1c: Save or copy a short clip you might want later.
l2c: Put the page title and the date you saw it in the same note.
l2d: You can keep the source with the clip.
l3c: Ask someone to find the source from your note, or show that you can.
safety: Do not save a private message you were not meant to keep.

name: Turn a headline into a question
description: Turn a headline into a question the article might answer, then see whether it does.
l1c: Rewrite the headline as one question.
l1d: You can turn a headline into a question.
l2c: Point to the sentence that answers it, or write that the piece does not.
l3c: If the piece answers a different question, write that question instead.
l3d: You can match the question to the piece.
safety: Do not add facts that are not in the piece.

name: Say when a number is rounded
description: Say whether a printed number is a count you could check or a round figure.
l1c: Write the number and the unit beside it.
l2c: Label it as a count, a round figure, or unknown, and point to the word that tells you.
l3n: Say what you would not do
l3c: Write one comparison you will not make until you know how it was rounded.
l3d: You can stop a weak comparison.
safety: Do not invent a more precise number.

name: Box the selling part
description: Draw a box around the part of a page that asks for money, a click, or a signup.
l1c: Point to the button, price, or sentence that asks you to act.
l2c: Draw one box around that part and leave the rest outside.
l3c: Say whether the text outside the box is still part of the offer.
safety: Do not sign up or pay as part of this practice.

name: Write what would change your mind
description: Write one observation that would make you drop a claim you currently hold.
l1c: Write the claim in one sentence.
l2c: Write one thing you could see or read that would make you drop it.
l3c: Ask whether someone else could see that thing, and rewrite it if they could not.
l3d: You can keep the test observable.
safety: Do not pick a test you know cannot be done.

name: Take an offer and add a fact
description: In a made-up scene, accept what the other person just said and add one new fact.
l1c: Repeat their fact in your next line without cancelling it.
l2c: Add one new fact that fits, and stop there.
l3n: Keep it on the next turn
l3c: When they respond, do not drop the fact you added.
safety: Stop if anyone is uncomfortable. This is play, not a confession.

name: Retell from the other seat
description: Tell a small real event again from the place of another person who was there.
l1c: Tell the event in under a minute from your place.
l2c: Tell it again using only what that other person could have seen or heard.
l3c: Name one thing you left out because that person could not have known it.
safety: Do not tell a story that exposes a private person.

name: Stop at the turn
description: Tell a short story and stop when it turns, then ask what the listener expects.
l1c: Mark the moment the situation changes.
l2c: Read or tell up to that moment and stop.
l2d: You can leave the ending open.
l3c: Ask what they expect next, then tell the rest and say what differed.
l3d: You can use a listener's guess.
safety: Do not trick someone with a story about them.

name: Describe a room by three sounds
description: Describe a room using three sounds, without naming an object you cannot hear.
l1c: Write three sounds you can hear from where you are.
l2c: Describe the room from those sounds and mark any object you did not hear.
l2d: You can stay with what you hear.
l3c: Read the description and ask where they think you are, then say what they could not know.
safety: Do not record a private conversation.

name: Change one rule and play
description: Change one rule of a game you already know, play one short round, and say what the change did.
l1c: Write the old rule and the one rule you changed.
l2c: Play one short round with the new rule.
l3c: Say one thing players did differently because of that rule.
safety: Use a game you may play. Do not add a dangerous physical challenge.

name: Give a character one want
description: Invent a character with one want and one obstacle, then play that for one minute.
l1c: Write one thing the character wants.
l2c: Write one obstacle that is not another new power.
l3c: Play or tell one minute in which the want meets the obstacle.
safety: Keep the play fictional and kind.

name: Order six sketches
description: Order six quick sketches so another person can say what happened.
l1c: Draw six rough frames of one small event.
l2c: Put them in an order and number the backs.
l3c: Ask someone what happened, then say which frame they misread.
l3d: You can see whether the order works.
safety: Do not draw a real private person in a mocking way.

name: Cut until the turn remains
description: Cut a short story until one turn remains, and read that version aloud.
l1c: Mark the sentence where the situation changes.
l2c: Remove sentences that do not lead to that turn or follow from it.
l3c: Read what remains and say what a listener still understands.
safety: Keep a copy of the longer version.

name: Hand over the next line
description: Stop your sentence and let the other person say the next line of a made-up scene.
l1c: Say one line that leaves room for a reply.
l2c: Stop before you answer your own line.
l3c: Continue from the line they actually said.
safety: Stop the game if someone wants to stop.

name: Set a scene with three objects
description: Place three objects and say what happened in the moment just before.
l1c: Place three objects where someone else can see them.
l2c: Tell what happened just before, using those objects.
l2d: You can tie the story to the objects.
l3c: Ask the other person for the next moment, using the same objects.
safety: Use objects you may handle.

name: Repeat a made-up fact
description: Repeat one invented fact in the same words when someone asks again later in the scene.
l1c: Say one invented fact once.
l2c: When asked, repeat that fact without adding a contradiction.
l2d: You can keep a fact stable.
l3c: If you change it, stop and correct it in the scene.
safety: Keep the fact fictional.

name: End on a picture
description: End a one-minute story on an image, not on a moral.
l1c: Tell a one-minute story with a clear last image.
l2c: Remove any last sentence that tells the listener what to think.
l2d: You can leave the meaning in the image.
l3c: Ask what picture stayed, and do not replace it with a lesson.
safety: Do not use a frightening image of a real person.

name: Answer as the character
description: Answer three questions in a character's voice without adding a new power.
l1c: Write what the character can know.
l2c: Answer three questions inside those limits.
l2d: You can stay in the voice.
l3c: Refuse one question the character could not answer, and say why.
l3d: You can stay inside the limit.
safety: This is play, not an impression of a private person.

name: Swap two events
description: Tell two events in the other order and say what the listener now believes.
l1c: Tell two events in the order they happened.
l2c: Tell the same facts in the other order.
l3c: Ask what the listener now thinks caused what, and write their answer.
l3d: You can see the effect of order.
safety: Use a harmless story.

name: Leave a prop for the next person
description: Leave one object and a one-line note so the next person can continue a scene.
l1c: Pick one object and write what it is in the story.
l2c: Write one line the next person can use.
l3c: Watch them add one beat, and do not correct them unless they ask.
l3d: You can hand a scene on.
safety: Use an object you may share.

name: Start from a sound
description: Start a one-minute story from a sound you just heard, and name the sound.
l1c: Write the sound you are using.
l2c: Tell one minute that begins with that sound.
l3c: At the end, point to the moment the sound mattered.
safety: Do not record anyone who did not agree.

name: Keep one reveal for the end
description: Hold one fact until the last line, and say why the story needed it there.
l1c: Write the fact you will hold.
l2c: Tell the story so it still makes sense before the last line.
l3c: Say the fact in the last line and ask whether it arrived too late to follow.
safety: Do not hide a fact someone needs for safety.

name: Read a year on a building
description: Read a year cut or fixed on a building and write one thing that year does not tell you.
l1c: Copy the year as it appears.
l1d: You can read a date stone.
l2c: Write one thing the year does not tell you about the building.
l3c: Write one question you would need another source to answer.
safety: Do not climb or lean out to read it.

name: Find one change in an old photo
description: Name one thing present in both an old photo and the place now, and one thing gone.
l1c: Point to one feature you can see in both.
l2c: Name one thing in the photo you cannot see now, or the reverse.
l3c: Mark one thing you are not sure is the same place.
safety: Use a photo you may study. Do not trespass to retake it.

name: Copy an inscription and mark a doubt
description: Copy a short inscription and mark any letter you are not sure of.
l1c: Copy one short line as it appears.
l2c: Circle one letter or word you are unsure about and say why.
l3c: Show that you did not add a letter the stone does not have.
l3d: You can keep the copy honest.
safety: Do not chalk or scratch the inscription.

name: Say who a memorial speaks to
description: Read a short memorial and say who it addresses.
l1c: Read the words that are actually there.
l2c: Say who the words speak to, from the words themselves.
l3c: Write one group or event the text does not mention.
safety: Be quiet and do not block the memorial.

name: Order objects by wear
description: Put three objects in order of wear and name the clue you used.
l1c: Choose three objects you may handle.
l2c: Put them in order from less worn to more worn.
l3c: Say the one clue you used, and one thing that clue does not prove.
safety: Do not damage an object to test it.

name: Mark a guess about a place name
description: Read a street or room name and write what it might refer to, marked as a guess.
l1c: Copy the name as signed.
l2c: Write what it might refer to, with the word guess.
l3c: Write where you would look to check it, or that you do not know.
l3d: You can leave a path to check.
safety: Do not present the guess as history.

name: Name one dating clue
description: Name one visible clue that places an old photo in time, and the limit of that clue.
l1c: Point to one thing in the photo you are using.
l2c: Say the range of time that clue suggests.
l3c: Write one reason the clue could mislead you.
safety: Do not claim a year the clue cannot support.

name: Separate a memory from a paper
description: Write one thing a person remembers and one thing a paper shows about the same event.
l1c: Write the remembered point in their words if you can.
l2c: Write one fact the paper shows.
l3c: Label which is which, and do not merge them into one sentence.
l3d: You can keep the two kinds apart.
safety: Ask before you write someone else's memory.

name: Copy a maker's mark
description: Find a maker's mark on a tool or dish and copy only what you can see.
l1c: Point to the maker's mark on the object.
l2c: Copy the letters or picture you can see.
l3c: Leave a blank where the mark is worn, instead of completing it.
safety: Do not scrape the mark to see it better.

name: Ask what a plaque does not say
description: Read a plaque and write one question it does not answer.
l1c: Summarize what it does say in one sentence.
l2c: Write one question a reader still has.
l3c: Say why that question changes how you use the plaque.
safety: Do not add a fact you did not check.

name: Find a changed word
description: Find one word that differs between two editions or printings of the same short text.
l1c: Put the two versions where you can see the same sentence.
l1d: You can set up the texts.
l2c: Mark one word that changed and write both words.
l3c: Write whether the change alters the sentence, or that you are not sure.
l3d: You can judge the change carefully.
safety: Use texts you may compare. Do not mark a library book.

name: Place a song with a named clue
description: Name one musical or lyric clue and the period it suggests, marked as a guess.
l1c: Write the clue you can actually hear or read.
l2c: Write the period you would guess, with the word guess.
l3c: Write what you would look up before you treated the guess as a date.
safety: Do not present the guess as a catalog date.

name: Copy an old spelling
description: Copy a historical name as printed, including a spelling you would not use now.
l1c: Copy the name letter for letter.
l2c: Do not modernize a letter in the copy.
l3c: On a separate line, write how you would spell it now, labeled as modern.
l3d: You can keep the two spellings apart.
safety: Do not correct the original.

name: Read a name on a bench
description: Read a dedication on a bench or similar gift and say what it does not tell you about the place.
l1c: Read the dedication that is there.
l2c: Say who or what the object is for, from the words.
l2d: You can say what it commemorates.
l3c: Write one thing about the place the dedication does not explain.
safety: Do not add flowers, marks, or objects.

name: Note a repair on an old object
description: Point to a repair on an old object and say what the repair tells you and what it does not.
l1c: Point to the mend, patch, or replaced part.
l2c: Say what the repair shows about use.
l3c: Say one thing the repair stops you from knowing about the original.
safety: Do not undo a repair.

name: Change one fold on a paper plane
description: Change one fold on a paper plane and say whether that flight went farther.
l1c: Fly the plane once and mark where it landed.
l1d: You can make a first flight.
l2c: Change one fold only, fly again, and say which landing was farther.
l3c: Say one thing besides the fold that also changed, such as your throw.
safety: Fly where you will not hit anyone.

name: Watch water appear on a glass
description: Watch a cold glass and say where water appeared on the outside.
l1c: Use a cold drink and note the outside is dry at the start, or say it is not.
l2c: Point to where water appears, and say whether it came from inside the glass.
l3c: Put a room-temperature glass beside it and say which one stays dry.
safety: Use a drink you may handle. Do not use boiling water.

name: Mark a puddle and return
description: Mark the edge of a puddle and note later the same day whether it is smaller.
l1c: Mark the edge with a stick or a note, without damaging the place.
l2c: Return later and say whether the edge has moved.
l3c: Write whether the spot was in sun or shade.
safety: Do not block a path.

name: Roll two shapes
description: Roll two different shapes down the same slope and say which went farther.
l1c: Use the same start line for both.
l1d: You can keep the start fair.
l2c: Roll each once and mark where it stops.
l3c: Say one reason the winner might change if you rolled again.
safety: Keep the roll away from people and stairs.

name: Tip a balanced ruler
description: Balance a ruler and move a small weight until it tips, then say where the weight was.
l1c: Balance the ruler on a finger or a pencil.
l1d: You can find a balance point.
l2c: Move one coin until the ruler tips, and mark that place.
l2d: You can find a tipping point.
l3c: Move the coin back and show the ruler balances again.
safety: Use a light ruler and a coin. Do not stand on anything.

name: Watch a salt solution
description: Leave a small salt solution and describe what you see the next day, without claiming a yield.
l1c: Dissolve salt in a little water in a shallow dish and write the start.
l2c: Describe what you see, including if you see nothing new.
l3n: Say what you will not claim
l3c: Write that you are not claiming a measured amount.
safety: Use table salt only. Do not taste the experiment. Keep it away from food.

name: Listen for an echo
description: Clap once in two places and say where you heard the clap come back.
l1c: Clap once and say whether you heard a repeat.
l1d: You can listen for a repeat.
l2c: Clap once in a second place and compare.
l3c: Say where the repeat was clearer, or that you heard none.
safety: Do not clap into someone's ear. Do not disturb a quiet place that asks for silence.

name: Bend two straw shapes
description: Bend drinking straws into two shapes and say which held a light book longer.
l1c: Make two different shapes from the same number of straws.
l2c: Rest the same light book on each and say which held.
l3c: Change one joint on the weaker shape and test again.
safety: Use straws and a light book. Do not stand on the model.

name: Overlap two color films
description: Overlap two pieces of colored transparent film and name the color you see.
l1c: Hold each film up and name its color.
l2c: Overlap them and name the color you see now.
l2d: You can see a mix of light.
l3c: Swap which film is in front and say whether the color changed.
safety: Use sweet wrappers or gels you may handle. Do not look at the sun through them.

name: Time two spinners
description: Make two paper spinners, change one thing, and say which spun longer.
l1c: Make two spinners that match.
l2c: Change the wing, the clip, or the drop on one spinner only.
l3c: Drop them from the same height and say which spun longer.
safety: Drop them where they cannot hit a face.

name: Fold a paper span
description: Span a gap with paper and add one fold so a light object can sit on it.
l1c: Lay a flat sheet across a small gap and see it sag.
l1d: You can see the flat sheet fail.
l2c: Add one fold or pleat and try the same light object.
l3c: Say how wide a gap you would not try with this sheet.
safety: Use paper and a light object such as an eraser. Do not stand on it.

name: Roll a ball on two floors
description: Roll the same ball on two surfaces and say which one slowed it sooner.
l1c: Use the same gentle push plan on both floors.
l1d: You can keep the start similar.
l2c: Mark where the ball stops on each surface.
l3c: Name the two surfaces in the note.
safety: Roll away from people and stairs.

name: Tap two lids
description: Tap two lids and say which one rings longer.
l1c: Tap one lid and listen until the sound dies.
l1d: You can listen to a ring.
l2c: Tap the other lid the same way and say which lasted longer.
l3c: Hold one lid in a different place and say how the sound changed.
safety: Tap lightly. Do not use broken lids.

name: Stretch a band and listen
description: Stretch a rubber band and say how the sound changed when you plucked it.
l1c: Pluck it once while it is loose and describe the sound.
l1d: You can hear the slack sound.
l2c: Stretch it farther and say what changed in the sound.
l3c: Let it slack again and say whether the first sound returned.
safety: Do not aim a stretched band at anyone, including yourself.

name: Weigh two shapes of the same clay
description: Shape the same piece of clay two ways and say whether the scale number stayed the same.
l1c: Weigh one shape and write the number.
l2c: Reshape that same clay and weigh it again.
l3c: Say that you did not add or remove clay, or note if you did.
l3d: You can account for the clay.
safety: Use a kitchen scale and clay you may handle. Do not bake it.

name: Drop a sheet and a crumple
description: Drop a flat sheet and a crumpled sheet of the same paper and say which landed first.
l1c: Drop it from shoulder height and watch the landing.
l2c: Crumple an equal sheet and drop it from the same height.
l3c: Say which landed first and one reason you would try again.
safety: Drop paper only, away from faces.

name: Slide a block on two surfaces
description: Slide the same small block on two surfaces and say which one stopped sooner.
l1c: Name the two surfaces before you start.
l2c: Use a similar start and mark where the block stops.
l3c: Wipe one surface and say whether the stop changed.
safety: Use a small block. Do not slide anything heavy.

name: See which way a spinner turns
description: Launch a simple spinner twice, once with each hand direction, and say which way it turned.
l1c: Spin it and say the direction you saw.
l2c: Change how you start it and say the new direction.
l3c: Write the start and the turn beside each other.
safety: Keep the spinner away from eyes.

name: Write a run of show
description: Write the start, one middle point, and the end time for a small gathering.
l1c: Write when it starts and what the first action is.
l2c: Write one middle point and who is responsible.
l3c: Write the end time where a newcomer could read it.
safety: Keep the plan shorter than the room can hold.

name: Name a backup person
description: Name who will do a job and who will do it if that person is late.
l1c: Write the person for one job.
l2c: Write a second person and tell them.
l3c: Write the moment the backup should step in.
safety: Ask both people before you publish their names.

name: Count chairs against a list
description: Count the chairs and say whether a named list of people can sit.
l1c: Count the chairs that are actually in the room.
l2c: Count the names on the list.
l3c: Say how many seats are short or spare, and what you will do about one of them.
l3d: You can act on the gap.
safety: Leave a path to the door.

name: Write where you go if it rains
description: Write in one sentence where the group goes if it rains, and how they will know.
l1c: Write the indoor or covered place.
l1d: You can name a backup place.
l2c: Write who decides and how people hear it.
l3c: Confirm the backup place is available, or write that you have not checked.
l3d: You can mark an unchecked plan.
safety: Do not plan a place you are not allowed to use.

name: Set a lost-and-found spot
description: Put one labeled spot for lost items and tell the group where it is.
l1c: Pick a spot people can see.
l2c: Label it so a stranger can tell what it is for.
l3c: Say or write the location before the event is underway.
safety: Do not leave valuables unattended as a test.

name: Note who has the key
description: Write who has the key or the responsibility to leave the room as agreed.
l1c: Write the name of the person who holds the key or the booking.
l2c: Write whether the room should be locked, unlocked, or left as you found it.
l3c: At the end, confirm that state and write that you did.
safety: Do not copy a key. Do not lock anyone in.

name: Read feedback cards
description: Collect one sentence from each person on a card and read the cards without ranking the people.
l1c: Give each person a card and one question.
l2c: Read the cards aloud or to yourself without adding a score.
l3c: Group two cards that mention the same thing, and leave the names off if they were optional.
safety: Do not require a name. Do not share a hurtful card.

name: Write what a late person needs
description: Write the one sentence a person who arrives late needs in order to join.
l1c: Write where to sit, what is happening, and who to ask.
l1d: You can write a joining note.
l2c: Place the note at the entrance you named.
l3c: Ask someone who missed the start whether the note was enough, or test it yourself.
safety: Do not single out a late person.

name: Post the end time
description: Put the end time where a person who just arrived can read it.
l1c: Write the end time in the form the group uses.
l2c: Put it by the entrance or the agenda, not only in a message someone may miss.
l3c: Show a newcomer the time without a speech.
safety: Use the time you actually agreed.

name: Agree a photo rule
description: Say what may be photographed before people arrive, and where that rule is written.
l1c: Write what is fine to photograph and what is not.
l2c: Place it where people see it as they enter.
l3c: Point to one moment where you followed it or asked.
safety: Do not photograph people who declined.

name: Make a readable name card
description: Write a name large enough to read from the other side of a table.
l1c: Write the name the person asked you to use.
l1d: You can write the requested name.
l2c: Read it from the other side of the table, or ask someone to.
l3c: Rewrite one card that failed the test.
safety: Ask each person how their name is written.

name: Give pairs one question
description: Pair people who have not already been talking, and give them one question.
l1c: Make pairs and say how you chose them.
l2c: Give the same question, written so they can read it.
l3c: Stop the pairs at the time you named.
safety: Let someone decline a pair.

name: Tick borrowed things back
description: List items the group borrowed and tick each one when it is back.
l1c: Write each borrowed item and its owner.
l2c: Tick an item only when you see it returned.
l3c: At the end, name any item still out and who has it.
safety: Do not mark an item returned if you have not seen it.

name: Write the speaking order
description: Write the order of three speakers and the sentence that hands the turn on.
l1c: Write three names in order.
l2c: Write the sentence the current speaker will use to pass the turn.
l3c: Use that sentence once and note whether the next person knew it was their turn.
safety: Agree the order with the speakers.

name: Match the room to the start
description: Take a photo at the start and leave the room matching it, or list what you changed on purpose.
l1c: Take one photo of the room before you move things.
l2c: Put items back, or write the changes the host allowed.
l3c: Look at the photo and the room together and say what still differs.
safety: Ask before you photograph a private room. Do not photograph people.

name: Put the agenda at the entrance
description: Place the agenda where a person entering can see it without asking.
l1c: Write three agenda lines a newcomer can read.
l1d: You can write a short agenda.
l2c: Put it at the entrance you are actually using.
l3c: See whether one person finds it without help, or move it if they do not.
safety: Do not block the door with the sign.

name: Leave a path to the door
description: Leave a clear path from the seats to the door, and show it to one person.
l1c: Walk from a seat to the door without moving a chair.
l2c: Move one thing that blocked the path, if you may.
l3c: Ask one person to walk it and say whether they had to turn sideways.
l3d: You can check with someone else.
safety: Do not block an exit. Do not move a permanent fixture.

name: Point with one arrow
description: Draw one arrow that touches the part you mean, and ask someone to name that part.
l1c: Circle nothing yet. Decide the one part.
l2c: Draw one arrow whose tip touches that part.
l2d: You can point with an arrow.
l3c: Ask someone which part you mean, and redraw the arrow if they miss.
safety: Use your own drawing or a photo you may mark.

name: Shoot from two heights
description: Take two photos of one object, one higher and one lower, and say what each shows.
l1c: Take one photo from above and say what you can see.
l2c: Take one photo from lower down and say what appeared.
l3c: Label each photo with the height so a viewer can tell them apart.
safety: Do not photograph a person who declined. Do not climb for the high view.

name: Label the one change
description: Show two images in the same frame and label the one thing that changed.
l1c: Take or draw two views with the same edges.
l2c: Change one thing and label it on the second image.
l3c: Ask someone what changed, and fix the label if they name something else.
safety: Do not stage a change that hides damage or danger.

name: Make the heading the only large type
description: Make one heading visibly larger than the body, and leave the body one size.
l1c: Write the body in one size.
l1d: You can set a body size.
l2c: Make one heading larger and nothing else.
l2d: You can give the heading the size.
l3c: Ask someone where their eye went first.
safety: Keep the text readable. Do not use a size you cannot read yourself.

name: Ask someone to name your mark
description: Draw a simple mark and write the word another person uses for it.
l1c: Draw a mark with no letters on it.
l2c: Show it and write the word they use.
l3c: Change the mark if their word was not the one you wanted, and test once more.
l3d: You can respond to the test.
safety: Do not use a mark that mocks a person.

name: Keep the label in the crop
description: Crop a photo and keep a label readable in the frame.
l1c: Point to the label that must stay.
l2c: Crop the photo and show the label still readable.
l2d: You can crop without losing the label.
l3c: Show one crop you rejected because the label was cut, if you made one.
l3d: You can reject a bad crop.
safety: Use a photo you may crop.

name: Use one color for the change
description: Use one color only for the thing that changed, and leave the rest in one other treatment.
l1c: Pick one color and write what it means.
l2c: Use it only on the change.
l3c: Ask someone what the color means, without telling them first.
safety: Do not rely on color alone if you can add a label.

name: Draw the hand on the step
description: Draw a hand on an object to show one step of a task.
l1c: Write the step in one line.
l2c: Draw the hand where it actually goes.
l3c: Ask someone to copy the step from the drawing, and note where the drawing failed.
safety: Show a safe, ordinary step. Do not draw a dangerous action.

name: Ask where the eye went
description: Place a title and ask someone where they looked first.
l1c: Put the title at the start of the path you intend.
l2c: Ask one person where they looked first, before you explain.
l3c: If they started elsewhere, move the title and ask again.
safety: Use your own page.

name: Put a known object for scale
description: Put a known object in the frame and say what size it gives the subject.
l1c: Choose an object whose size a viewer knows.
l2c: Photograph or draw it in the same plane as the subject.
l2d: You can put it in the frame.
l3c: Say one way the scale could still mislead.
safety: Do not use a person's body if they did not agree.

name: Number steps on one drawing
description: Number three steps on one drawing in the order they are done.
l1c: Draw one view that can hold the steps.
l2c: Write 1, 2, and 3 on the drawing in the order of the work.
l3c: Ask someone to point to the steps in order, and fix a number that misled them.
safety: Use an ordinary task. Do not number a dangerous procedure.

name: Remove a mark that does not explain
description: Remove one decorative mark from a diagram and say what became clearer.
l1c: Point to a mark that does not explain a step.
l2c: Take it off a copy, not the only original.
l3c: Show the two versions and say what a viewer can see now.
safety: Keep the original.

name: Caption the change
description: Write a caption that says what changed, not how you feel about it.
l1c: Write one sentence that names the change.
l2c: Remove a word that only praises or complains.
l2d: You can keep the caption factual.
l3c: Ask someone to point to the change from the caption alone.
safety: Do not hide a change that matters to safety.

name: Record their word for a symbol
description: Show a symbol and write the word the other person used, even if it is not yours.
l1c: Show it without saying your word.
l2c: Write the word they said.
l3c: Keep your symbol, add their word, or redraw, and say which you did.
safety: Do not argue them out of the word before you write it.

name: Show every step of one example
description: Write one worked example with every step visible, including the last result.
l1c: Choose a task of a few steps you can finish.
l2c: Write each step so a reader can see it.
l3c: Ask someone which step they had to guess, and add that step.
safety: Use a safe, ordinary task.

name: Mark which answer used the notes
description: Write three questions, answer them, and mark which answer used the notes.
l1c: Write three questions about one page.
l1d: You can write a short check.
l2c: Answer them, and mark the one that needed the notes.
l2d: You can see where notes mattered.
l3c: Answer the same three later without the notes and say which you lost.
safety: Use your own notes.

name: Show the line that fixes a step
description: Show one wrong step and the line that fixes it.
l1c: Write a step with one clear error.
l2c: Write the corrected line beside it.
l3c: Cover the labels and ask someone to pick the fix.
safety: Use a harmless example, not a safety procedure.

name: Watch them do the next step
description: Stop an explanation and let the learner do the next step while you watch.
l1c: Stop before the last step.
l2c: Watch them do it without taking over.
l3c: Write the one hint you gave, or that you gave none.
safety: Let them decline. Use a safe step.

name: Write the question that returned
description: When a learner asks the same question again, stop and write that question down.
l1c: Point to the question the second time it appears.
l2c: Write it in their words.
l3c: Answer it in a different way, or say you need to learn it first.
l3d: You can respond to the repeat.
safety: Do not treat the repeated question as a fault.

name: Name tomorrow's practice
description: Write the one thing you will practice next, and where you will do it.
l1c: Write one action, not a topic.
l2c: Write where and roughly when.
l3c: After that time, write whether you did it.
safety: Choose a practice you can actually do.

name: Pick the explanation you can use
description: Read two short explanations and say which one you can follow without the author present.
l1c: Read two explanations of the same idea.
l2c: Follow one of them on a real example.
l3c: Say which one you could use alone, and the point where the other lost you.
safety: Do not copy the explanations out at length.

name: Log a mistake and its cue
description: Write three mistakes you made on a task and the cue that would have stopped each one.
l1c: Write three mistakes from one piece of work.
l2c: Beside each, write the cue that would have stopped it.
l3c: On the next try, use one of those cues and say whether the mistake returned.
safety: Keep the log private if it names other people.

name: Teach with the object in their hands
description: Teach one step while the object is in the learner's hands, not yours.
l1c: Give them the object before you explain.
l1d: You can give them the object.
l2c: Guide one step with words while they hold it.
l2d: You can teach from their hands.
l3c: Let them finish that step and say what you were about to grab.
l3d: You can keep your hands off.
safety: Use a safe object. Do not teach a dangerous step this way.

name: Ask what they expect
description: Ask what the learner thinks will happen, then show the result.
l1c: Write their expectation before you demonstrate.
l2c: Do the ordinary action and show what happened.
l2d: You can compare with the result.
l3c: Ask them what differed from their guess.
safety: Use a harmless demonstration.

name: Write a hint that points
description: Write a hint that says where to look, not the answer.
l1c: Write where to look or which step to retry.
l2c: Read it and remove any word that gives the result.
l2d: You can keep the answer out.
l3c: Give it to someone who is stuck and see whether they move without the answer.
safety: Do not withhold help someone needs for safety.

name: Try the step on a new case
description: Give a new example and see whether the learner uses the same step.
l1c: Finish one example together.
l1d: You can complete a first case.
l2c: Give a new case that needs the same step.
l3c: Say whether they used the step, and where the new case differed.
safety: Keep the new case safe and ordinary.

name: Cover the answer and try
description: Cover a worked answer, try the step, then uncover and compare.
l1c: Cover the result before you start.
l2c: Do the step and write your result.
l2d: You can try without the answer.
l3c: Uncover and mark what differed.
safety: Use your own practice page.

name: Write the step in their words
description: Ask the learner to say the step, and write it in their words.
l1c: Let them describe the step before you rewrite it.
l2c: Write what they said, not your preferred sentence.
l3c: Add one missing piece only if they agree it was missing.
safety: Do not correct their wording before you have written it.

name: Write the time back
description: After you agree a time, write it back and ask the other person to correct it.
l1c: Write the day and time in the form you both used.
l1d: You can send the time back.
l2c: Ask them to change it if it is wrong.
l3c: Keep their confirmation or their change with the note.
safety: Do not announce a time they have not seen.

name: Stop after two options
description: Offer two times or two choices, then stop talking.
l1c: Name two real options and no third one.
l2c: Do not add a third while they are choosing.
l3c: Write the one they chose, or that they chose neither.
safety: Make both options ones you can actually do.

name: Repeat the no
description: When someone declines, repeat the no and do not add a new offer in the same breath.
l1c: Point to the words they used to decline.
l2c: Repeat the no in a short sentence without a new proposal.
l2d: You can leave the no standing.
l3c: Wait for them to reopen the subject, or end the topic.
safety: Do not pressure someone who has declined.

name: Name the idea you oppose
description: Say the idea you disagree with and one reason, without a remark about the person.
l1c: Write the idea in words they would recognize.
l2c: Add one reason that is about the idea.
l3c: Read it and delete any comment about their character.
l3d: You can keep it on the idea.
safety: Stop if the conversation is not yours to join.

name: Ask what they want from you
description: Ask whether they want a listener, a suggestion, or help, before you offer a fix.
l1c: Ask which of those they want.
l1d: You can ask for the job.
l2c: Wait for the answer before you advise.
l3c: Do the job they named, or say you cannot.
safety: Do not turn a request for listening into advice.

name: Write the owner of the decision
description: Write the decision and the one person who will carry it.
l1c: Write what was decided in one sentence.
l2c: Write one name, and check they accept it.
l3c: Write what others will see when it is done.
safety: Do not assign someone who is not in the room without asking.

name: Name the next speaker
description: Stop and name the person who has the next turn.
l1c: Stop at the end of your point.
l2c: Say their name and that the turn is theirs.
l2d: You can hand the turn over.
l3c: Do not add a second point while they start.
safety: Do not name someone who asked not to speak.

name: Write what you will not do
description: Write what you will not do, in one sentence the other person can repeat.
l1c: Write one boundary as an action you will not take.
l2c: Ask them to say it back.
l2d: You can check they heard it.
l3c: If you are about to cross it, stop and point to the sentence.
safety: A boundary is not a threat. Do not punish someone for hearing it.

name: Stop your own sentence
description: Stop your sentence when someone else starts, and let them finish.
l1c: Stop when their voice starts.
l2c: Do not restart until they have finished the point.
l3c: Ask if they want your point, or drop it.
safety: Do not treat this as a rule for unsafe interruptions.

name: Read the decision back
description: Read the decision back in their words before you leave.
l1c: Write the decision using words they used.
l1d: You can stay with their words.
l2c: Read it aloud before you end.
l3c: Change the sentence if they say it is wrong.
safety: Do not leave with an unconfirmed decision on a shared task.

name: Ask a closed question, then an open one
description: Ask one yes-or-no question, then one question that needs a sentence.
l1c: Ask one question that can be answered yes or no.
l1d: You can ask a closed question.
l2c: Ask one question that needs more than yes or no.
l2d: You can follow with an open question.
l3c: Write both answers and say which one you will act on.
safety: Do not stack more questions before they answer.

name: Say the assumption aloud
description: Say the assumption the plan depends on, and ask if it is still true.
l1c: Write the one assumption in a sentence.
l2c: Ask the other person if it is still true.
l3c: Write what you will change if it is not true.
safety: Do not hide an assumption that affects someone else.

name: Write when you will check again
description: Write when you will look at a task again, and what will count as done.
l1c: Write the day or the event that triggers the check.
l2c: Write the visible sign of done.
l3c: At that time, write whether it is done.
safety: Choose a check you control.

name: Name who changed the decision
description: Say whose point changed a decision, in front of the people who were there.
l1c: Say the point that changed the decision.
l2c: Say who brought that point.
l3c: Repeat the decision so the credit does not replace it.
safety: Credit only a point that was actually used.

name: Offer a smaller step
description: When a task stalls, offer one smaller step the other person can accept or refuse.
l1c: Say where the task stopped.
l2c: Offer one smaller step, not a new plan.
l3c: Do that step only if they want it, or stop.
safety: Do not take over the task.

name: Separate the fact you both see
description: Write one fact you can both point to, separate from what each of you prefers.
l1c: Write a fact both of you can see or reread.
l1d: You can find a shared fact.
l2c: Write each preference on a different line.
l3n: Ask if the fact is right
l3c: Ask them to correct the fact before you discuss the preference.
safety: This does not settle a dispute. It only separates the fact.

name: Rinse a brush until the water runs clear
description: Rinse a paintbrush and stop when the water runs clear.
l1c: Rinse the brush in water until you can see the color leave.
l2c: Change the water and stop when a rinse stays clear.
l2d: You can see a clear rinse.
l3c: Leave the bristles in their shape and say where you will put the brush.
safety: Use water-based paint. Do not pour thick paint down a drain.

name: Mend a tear from the back
description: Mend a torn page from the back so the text on the front stays readable.
l1c: Put the tape or tissue on the back of a scrap or a page you may mend.
l1d: You can mend from the back.
l2c: Show that the words on the front can still be read.
l3c: Trim tape that covers a word, or say you need a thinner mend.
safety: Do not mend a page you were told not to alter.

name: Ease an edge until cloth passes
description: Smooth one rough edge until a cloth passes over it without catching.
l1c: Pull a cloth across the edge and show where it catches.
l2c: Sand or file only that spot.
l3c: Pull the cloth again and stop when it passes.
safety: Wear no loose cloth near a moving tool. Use a hand file or sandpaper only.

name: Oil a dry spoon and wipe it
description: Rub food-safe oil on a dry wooden spoon and wipe off the excess.
l1c: Show the spoon is clean and dry.
l1d: You can start from dry wood.
l2c: Rub on a little oil and wipe until the surface is not wet.
l3c: Write the oil you used, from the container.
safety: Use an oil sold for wood that touches food. Do not oil a spoon that is still wet or soiled.

name: Press one leaf and date it
description: Press one fallen leaf flat and write the date you will look at it again.
l1c: Use a leaf that has already fallen.
l2c: Put it in a book or press with a note of the date.
l3c: On the date you wrote, say whether it stayed flat.
safety: Do not pick a living plant. Do not press a leaf that irritates skin.

name: Bind a cord end
description: Bind the end of a cord so it does not fray, then tug the binding.
l1c: Wrap the end so the strands are covered.
l2c: Tug the binding and say whether it slipped.
l3c: If it slips, wrap it again and tug once more.
safety: Use cord you may practice on. Keep the knife, if you use one, away from the holding hand.

name: Sew a short hem
description: Sew a short hem on scrap cloth with stitches you can point to.
l1c: Fold the edge and hold it.
l2c: Sew a short length with stitches you can see.
l3c: Point to one stitch and say what it holds.
safety: Use a needle with care. Do not sew clothing someone is wearing.

name: Choose a closer thread
description: Choose a thread closer in color to a cloth than another thread, and say why.
l1c: Lay two thread colors on the cloth.
l2c: Pick the closer one and say the reason in the light you are using.
l3c: Look again in a different light and say whether you would still choose it.
safety: Use thread and cloth you may handle.

name: Rest a brush so the bristles stay straight
description: Put a damp brush where the bristles are not bent, and look at it the next day.
l1c: Lay or hang it so the bristles do not press on a point.
l2c: Say whether the bristles are still straight.
l3c: If they bent, show the new place you will use.
safety: Do not leave a wet brush on a surface it will stain.

name: Hang a bundle where air reaches
description: Tie a small bundle of herbs or flowers so air can reach it, and hang it where you said.
l1c: Tie the bundle so you can see gaps.
l1d: You can tie a loose bundle.
l2c: Write where it will hang.
l3c: Hang it in that place and show the gaps are still open.
safety: Use plants you may cut. Do not dry plants you cannot identify if you might eat them.

name: Wax a thread and sew an inch
description: Wax a short thread and sew one inch so the thread does not tangle.
l1c: Draw the thread across wax once.
l2c: Sew a short line on scrap cloth.
l3c: Say whether it tangled less than an unwaxed end you tried.
safety: Use a needle carefully.

name: Patch paper from behind
description: Patch a small paper hole from behind and write on the front.
l1c: Put paper behind the hole.
l2c: Write one word across the mend.
l3c: Say whether the mend is for practice or for a page you may alter.
safety: Do not alter a document you must keep clean.

name: Coil a hose with the end on top
description: Coil a hose or cable so the end you need is on top and it does not kink.
l1c: Make a coil without a sharp kink.
l2c: Finish with the end you will use on top.
l2d: You can leave the end ready.
l3c: Pull a short length and show the coil does not knot.
safety: Use an empty hose or a light cable. Do not open a water fitting.

name: Note the light on a color sample
description: Label a color sample with the light you viewed it in.
l1c: Look at the sample in one light and name that light.
l2c: Write the light on the sample or its note.
l3c: Look at it in a second light and say whether you would still call it the same.
l3d: You can see the light change.
safety: Do not rely on the sample for a safety color without a label.

name: Check a strip at both ends
description: Cut one strip along a guide and measure the width at both ends.
l1c: Cut one strip using a ruler or a folded guide.
l1d: You can cut with a guide.
l2c: Write the width at each end.
l3c: Say whether the ends match closely enough for your use.
safety: Cut away from your fingers. Use paper or card.

name: Stitch a pamphlet so it opens
description: Stitch a few sheets into a pamphlet that opens and stays together.
l1c: Fold the sheets together.
l2c: Sew through the fold so the pages hold.
l3c: Open the pamphlet and show a page turning without falling out.
safety: Use a needle with care and scrap paper.

name: Follow a brush label or stop
description: Clean a brush only in the way its label describes, or stop if there is no label.
l1c: Find the care line, or write that there is none.
l1d: You can look for a label.
l2c: Follow that line, or do nothing if it is missing.
l2d: You can stop without a label.
l3n: Say what you did not do
l3c: Write one cleaner you did not use because the label did not name it.
l3d: You can refuse an extra chemical.
safety: Do not mix cleaners. Do not invent a solvent.

name: File a snag until cloth passes
description: File one snag on a piece of wood until a cloth passes over it.
l1c: Show the point where cloth catches.
l2c: File only the spot where the cloth caught.
l3c: Pull cloth across it and stop when it no longer catches.
safety: File away from your hand. Do not use a power tool.

name: Sort screws by the head you can see
description: Sort a small mix of screws by the head you can see, into labeled cups.
l1c: Label cups with the head shapes you actually have.
l2c: Put each screw in the cup that matches its head.
l3c: Put one unclear screw aside instead of forcing it.
safety: Do not sort by forcing a driver into a head.

name: Test glue on a scrap
description: Test a glue on a scrap of the same material before you use it on the real piece.
l1c: Use a scrap of the same material.
l1d: You can make a test piece.
l2c: Glue the scrap and wait as the container says, or stop if it gives no time.
l3c: Try to separate the scrap and say whether you will use that glue on the real piece.
l3d: You can decide from the test.
safety: Use glue as the container says. Do not heat it. Keep it off skin.

name: Sketch posture without naming a species
description: Sketch a bird or animal's posture and write that you are not naming the species.
l1c: Draw the posture you see, not a field-guide copy.
l2c: Write that the sketch is not an identification.
l3c: Add one clue you saw, labeled as a clue rather than a name.
safety: Do not approach or feed the animal. Do not use a call to draw it in.

name: Count calls and write the place
description: Count calls for a short, stated time and write the place and the hour.
l1c: Write the length of time before you start.
l2c: Count the calls and write the number with the place.
l3c: If you hear two kinds, write them apart or say you did not separate them.
l3d: You can be honest about the count.
safety: Do not play calls to provoke animals.

name: Note which way a tree leans
description: Note which way a tree leans and what stands beside it.
l1c: Name a landmark you can use as a direction.
l2c: Write which way the trunk leans relative to that landmark.
l3c: Write what is beside the trunk, such as a wall or an open side.
safety: Do not climb the tree.

name: Compare two marks and stop
description: Say which of two marks looks sharper, and what you will not conclude about what made them.
l1c: Say which mark looks sharper or newer.
l2c: Write one conclusion you will not draw.
l3c: Write what the ground was like.
safety: Do not follow an animal. Do not touch a mark you cannot identify.

name: Note open and closed blooms
description: Note which blooms on one plant are open and which are closed at two times of day.
l1c: Write the time and what is open.
l1d: You can make a first note.
l2c: Write a later time and what changed.
l3c: Show that you did not pick a bloom for the note.
safety: Do not pick flowers. Watch from a path.

name: Show the place matches the start
description: List or photograph a spot before you use it, then show it matches when you leave.
l1c: Make a short list or a photo of the spot.
l2c: Do your ordinary activity without adding a mark.
l3c: Show the spot against the start and name anything you removed.
safety: Do not photograph people. Pack out what you brought.

name: Show what you carried out
description: Show that what you carried out of a place matches what you brought in, plus any litter you meant to remove.
l1c: List what is in the bag at the start.
l2c: List it again at the end.
l3c: Explain any item that was added or used.
l3d: You can account for a change.
safety: Do not take plants, stones, or artifacts.

name: Draw one landmark on the skyline
description: Draw a skyline and mark one landmark you could find again.
l1c: Draw the horizon you see.
l2c: Mark one building, hill, or tree you can name or describe.
l3c: From the same spot, point to that landmark using the drawing.
safety: Do not block a path to draw.

name: Name the wind by a landmark
description: Write where the wind came from by pointing to a landmark, not a guessed degree.
l1c: Face the wind and name the landmark it comes from.
l2c: Write the landmark and the time.
l3c: Check again a little later and say whether it still matches.
safety: Do not look at the sun to judge the wind.

name: Measure one plant and date it
description: Measure one plant against a ruler and write the date.
l1c: Write the height you measured and where you put the ruler.
l2c: Write the date beside the number.
l3c: Measure again on a later day and say what changed, or that you have not returned yet.
l3d: You can set up a second measure.
safety: Do not pull the plant up to measure it.

name: Mark three sounds on a line
description: Draw a short walk as a line and mark three sounds where you heard them.
l1c: Draw the walk with a start and an end.
l2c: Mark three sounds at the place on the line where you heard them.
l3c: Walk or recall the line and say whether the order matches.
safety: Do not record other people's conversations.

name: Name what you will leave
description: Name one thing you could take and then leave it where it is.
l1c: Point to the thing and say you will leave it.
l1d: You can choose to leave it.
l2c: Show it still there when you go.
l3c: Write one reason it stays, such as a rule or a living plant.
safety: Do not take natural or historical objects.

name: Note two sides of a path
description: Write one difference between the two sides of a path.
l1c: Choose one spot on the path.
l2c: Write one difference you can see between the two sides.
l3n: Say what you will not infer
l3c: Write one cause you will not claim from that difference.
safety: Stay on the path.

name: Watch a cloud shadow cross
description: Watch a cloud shadow cross the ground and say which way it went.
l1c: Point to a shadow on the ground, not at the sun.
l2c: Say which landmark it moved toward.
l3c: Write the time and the landmark.
safety: Do not look at the sun.

name: Show what you moved
description: Photograph or list a setting before you change it, then show what you moved.
l1c: Make a photo or a list before the change.
l2c: Move one thing and leave the rest where it was.
l3c: Show the before and after and name the thing you moved.
safety: Ask before you change a shared space. Do not photograph people.

name: Keep an original unchanged
description: Save a copy under a new name and show that the original file or page did not change.
l1c: Write the name of the original.
l2c: Save the copy under a different name.
l3c: Open the original and show a mark you did not add.
safety: Do not overwrite the only copy.

name: Write the version on the page
description: Write a version mark on a page and say what changed from the previous one.
l1c: Write a version such as first or second on the page.
l2c: Write one thing that changed.
l3c: Show the earlier page still exists.
safety: Do not throw away the earlier version as part of the exercise.

name: Move a finished draft aside
description: Move a draft you are finished with into a place you named, and leave a working file separate.
l1c: Write the folder or envelope for finished drafts.
l2c: Move the finished draft there.
l3c: Show the file you are still changing, separate from the finished one.
safety: Do not delete the finished draft.

name: Open the file you sent
description: Open the file you sent and match one sentence to the draft you meant to send.
l1c: Open the copy that actually went, not the folder you think you used.
l1d: You can open the sent file.
l2c: Find one sentence that matches the draft.
l3c: If something differs, write the difference before you send a correction.
safety: Do not send a file to test this on an unwilling person.

name: Write what you did not change
description: Write three lines: what changed, why, and what you left alone.
l1c: Name the change in one line.
l2c: Write the reason in one line.
l3c: Name one part you did not change.
safety: Keep the note with the file.

name: Edit only the new page
description: Mark one page as finished and make the next change only on a new page.
l1c: Write that the page is finished.
l2c: Make the next edit on a new page.
l2d: You can leave the finished page.
l3c: Show the finished page without the new marks.
safety: Do not sneak a change onto the finished page.

name: Pick the latest name, then open it
description: Choose the latest of three files from the date in the name, then open it to check.
l1c: Read the three names without opening them.
l2c: Say which name looks latest.
l2d: You can choose from the name.
l3c: Open it and say whether the content matches that date.
safety: Use practice files, not someone else's private files.

name: Save a link under your title
description: Save a link with a title you wrote, not only the title the page gave you.
l1c: Write a title that says why you saved it.
l2c: Save the address with that title.
l3c: Find the link from your title later the same day.
safety: Do not save a private link you should not keep.

name: Write what done looks like
description: Write the visible sign of done before you start a small task.
l1c: Write what you will see when it is done.
l2c: Do the task you defined before you started.
l3c: Point to the sign, or say it is not done yet.
safety: Choose a task you can finish.

name: Undo the last change
description: Undo the last change on a practice page or file and show the previous state.
l1c: Make one change you can reverse.
l2c: Reverse that change only.
l3c: Show the page or file as it was.
safety: Practice on a copy if the work matters.

name: Name the missing piece
description: Name the piece you are missing and the place you already looked.
l1c: Write the name of the piece you do not have.
l2c: Write the places you already looked for it.
l3c: Ask for the piece using its name and where you looked.
safety: Do not take a replacement that does not fit without checking.

name: Write the limit first
description: Write the one limit on a task, then do the task inside it.
l1c: Write the time, the material, or the rule before you start.
l2c: Do the task without crossing the limit.
l3c: If you hit the limit, stop and write what is unfinished.
l3d: You can stop at the limit.
safety: Choose a limit that keeps the task safe.

name: Stop when the question is answered
description: Stop a piece of work when the result answers the question you wrote down.
l1c: Write the question before you continue.
l2c: Point to the part of the result that answers it.
l3c: Stop adding, and write what you did not add.
safety: Do not stop early if the missing part is a safety check you already planned.

name: List what stays
description: List two things that will stay the same, then change one other thing.
l1c: Write two things you will not change.
l2c: Change one other thing only.
l3c: Show that the two stayed.
safety: Use a practice piece if the original matters.

name: Write the question before you search
description: Write the question on paper before you open a search.
l1c: Write one question you can finish.
l2c: Search only for that question.
l2d: You can keep the search narrow.
l3c: Write the answer with where you found it, or write that you did not find it.
safety: Do not invent a page you did not open.

name: Rehearse the cut on scrap
description: Make the cut on a scrap before you cut the piece you mean to keep.
l1c: Cut the scrap with the same guide.
l2c: Say what you would change.
l2d: You can learn from the scrap.
l3c: Cut the real piece only if the scrap worked, otherwise stop.
safety: Cut paper or card, away from your fingers. Do not use a power saw.

name: Mark a line tools will not cross
description: Mark a line on the table and keep tools on the work side of it.
l1c: Put a tape or a pencil line where tools should stop.
l2c: Do a small task and keep tools on one side.
l3c: Show whether any tool crossed, and put it back if it did.
safety: Do not put the line across an exit.

name: Sit where they can see you
description: Sit where the person you are with can see your face without turning sharply.
l1c: Ask where they would like you to sit.
l2c: Sit there, or explain the one seat you cannot use.
l3c: Ask if they can see you well enough to talk.
safety: Do not move someone else's chair without asking.

name: Ask before you move their object
description: Ask before you move an object that belongs to the person you are helping.
l1c: Point to the object and say what you want to do.
l2c: Wait for a yes, or leave it.
l3c: If you moved it, put it back where they asked.
safety: Do not tidy someone else's things unasked.

name: Leave a note in their words
description: Leave a short note using words the person chose for what they need.
l1c: Ask what the note should say.
l2c: Write those words, not a paraphrase they did not hear.
l3c: Read it back and change it if they ask.
safety: Do not leave a note about their health or private affairs.

name: Agree a break signal
description: Agree a signal that means pause, and use it once.
l1c: Agree a word or a gesture.
l2c: Use it once and stop the activity.
l3c: Wait for them to restart.
safety: A signal is not a medical instruction.

name: Invite the quiet person once
description: Invite a person who has not spoken, once, and accept it if they do not take the turn.
l1c: Offer the turn once by name.
l2c: Leave a pause long enough for an answer.
l3c: If they do not speak, continue without a second push.
safety: Do not comment on their silence.

name: Stop a joke that leaves someone out
description: Stop a joke you were telling when you see it leaves someone out.
l1c: Stop the joke before the ending.
l2c: Say you are stopping because it leaves someone out.
l2d: You can give a short reason.
l3c: Move to a subject that includes the person.
safety: Do not repeat the joke to explain it.

name: Close a gap in the circle
description: Move your own chair so a person can join the circle without climbing over anyone.
l1c: Point to the gap a new person would need.
l2c: Move your own chair to open that gap.
l3c: Offer the seat and leave it if they refuse.
safety: Do not pull someone into the circle.

name: Write a question for the meeting
description: Write one question you could ask at a public meeting, and what answer would help.
l1c: Write one question in one or two sentences.
l2c: Write what kind of answer would help you act.
l2d: You can say what you need.
l3c: Say whether the question matches an item on the agenda, or that you have not seen the agenda.
safety: Do not present the question as advice on how to vote.

name: Read a closing date
description: Read a closing date on a notice and say what closes on that date.
l1c: Point to the closing date printed on the notice.
l2c: Say whether it is a form, a booking, a show, or something else the notice names.
l3c: Write the one action you would take before that date, or that the notice is not for you.
safety: Do not miss a date by guessing. Read the notice.

name: Find where a form goes back
description: Find where a form should be returned, from the form itself.
l1c: Point to the line that says where it goes.
l2c: Copy the address, box, or office as written.
l3c: If the form does not say, write that you would ask before sending it.
l3d: You can stop when it is missing.
safety: Do not send the form as a practice.

name: Compare two sets of hours
description: Compare the hours of two nearby services and say which one is open at a time you name.
l1c: Write both sets of hours from the signs or pages.
l2c: Name a time and say which service is open then.
l3c: Note one day one of them is closed.
safety: Use posted hours. Do not assume a holiday.

name: Read a rule on a door
description: Read a rule posted on a door and say what you will do because of it.
l1c: Read the rule that is posted.
l2c: Say the action you will take or avoid.
l3c: If it conflicts with another sign, say you will ask rather than choose.
l3d: You can stop on a conflict.
safety: Follow the posted rule.

name: Read a ratio as parts
description: Read a ratio such as one to four and say what one part means in the thing you are looking at.
l1c: Write the two numbers and what they refer to.
l2c: Say what one part is, using the label.
l3n: Stop if the label is unclear
l3c: If the label does not say, write that you will not mix or measure from it.
safety: Do not mix chemicals, medicines, or cleaners from a ratio.

name: Check a walked distance
description: Walk a distance you estimated in paces, then check it against a known measure.
l1c: Write how many paces you think a short marked distance will take.
l2c: Walk it and write the paces you took.
l2d: You can count a real walk.
l3c: Compare with the marked distance and say whether your pace guess was long or short.
safety: Walk where you are allowed. Do not walk into a road to finish a count.

name: Read the time left
description: Read how much time is left until a moment you can see on a clock.
l1c: Name the time you are counting toward.
l2c: Read the clock and say how much time is left.
l3c: Look again near the end and say whether your first reading still fits.
safety: Use a clock you can see. Do not guess the time from memory.

name: Pin a hem before you sew
description: Pin a hem on scrap cloth, check the length, then sew or unpin.
l1c: Pin the fold so it stays.
l2c: Measure or look at the length and move a pin if it is uneven.
l3c: Sew only if the pins are right, otherwise unpin and say why.
safety: Point pins away from the hand that holds the cloth.

name: Fold a scarf so the ends meet
description: Fold or hang a scarf so the ends meet where you intended.
l1c: Say where the ends should meet.
l2c: Arrange the scarf so the ends meet there.
l3c: Move, then fix the ends if they slipped.
safety: Use your own scarf.

name: Find a repeat in a tune
description: Find a phrase that comes back in a tune you can sing or play slowly.
l1c: Sing or play a short tune you already know.
l2c: Point to the moment a phrase comes back.
l3c: Sing the returning phrase on its own.
safety: Use a tune you may sing. Do not claim a recording right you do not have.

name: Mark a rest while you clap
description: Clap a short pattern that includes a silence you can point to.
l1c: Clap a pattern of a few beats.
l2c: Leave one silence and point to it.
l3c: Ask someone to clap it back, including the silence.
l3d: You can pass the rest on.
safety: Keep the volume kind to the room.

name: Name a loud and a soft moment
description: In a piece of music or a room, name one louder moment and one softer moment.
l1c: Point to a moment that is louder than what is around it.
l1d: You can hear a louder moment.
l2c: Point to a softer moment.
l2d: You can hear a softer moment.
l3c: Say what you compared them with.
safety: Do not turn music up to test this. Protect your hearing.

name: Follow a repeat mark
description: Follow a printed repeat on a simple line of music or a rhythm line, and stop where it says.
l1c: Point to the repeat mark.
l2c: Do the line again where the mark says.
l3c: Stop at the place the line now ends.
safety: Use beginner notation you may practice. Miss nothing that would strain your voice.

name: Stack the talking piece
description: Use one object as a talking piece and pass it before the next person speaks.
l1c: Put one object in the middle and say what it means.
l2c: Speak only while you hold it, once.
l3c: Hand it to the next person and stop.
l3d: You can give the turn away.
safety: Let someone speak without the object if they need to leave or to stop the activity.

name: Write their words on a parking list
description: When a topic is parked, write it in the speaker's words.
l1c: Say that the topic is parked.
l2c: Write the topic as they said it.
l3c: Bring one parked item back at the time you named, or say you ran out of time.
safety: Do not rewrite their point before they see it.

name: Repeat the word they used
description: Repeat the feeling or importance word they used, without adding your own.
l1c: Note the word they chose.
l2c: Use that word in your reply.
l3c: Ask whether that word still fits.
safety: Do not diagnose a feeling.

name: Set a sample before the batch
description: Make or show one sample and get a yes before you make the rest.
l1c: Finish one sample of the ordinary thing.
l2c: Ask the other person if that sample is the one to repeat.
l3c: Make the rest only after a yes, or stop.
l3d: You can wait for the yes.
safety: Use a harmless craft or paper task, not food for someone with an allergy you have not asked about.

name: Label left and right on a photo
description: Label the left and right of a photo from the viewer's side, and say whose left you mean.
l1c: Write whether you mean the viewer's left or the subject's left.
l2c: Mark that side on a copy.
l3c: Ask someone to point to the side you named.
safety: Use a photo you may mark. Do not label a person's body without consent.

name: Trace a crack you will not fill
description: Trace the path of a crack on a note or a photo, and do not fill it.
l1c: Draw the crack's path on a copy or a note.
l2c: Mark where you can see it start and stop.
l3c: Write that you did not fill, glue, or paint it.
safety: Do not stand on a damaged step. Do not open a wall.

name: Make a rubbing of a coin
description: Make a rubbing of a coin you may use, and say which side you rubbed.
l1c: Put the coin under the paper.
l2c: Rub until the picture shows, and stop before the paper tears.
l3c: Write which side of the coin it is.
safety: Use your own coin. Do not rub a fragile object or a monument.

name: Tie a luggage label that stays
description: Tie a label to a bag so it stays on when you lift the bag.
l1c: Write a name or a code you are willing to show.
l2c: Tie the label to a handle so it can be lifted.
l3c: Lift the bag once and show the label stayed.
safety: Do not put a full home address on a label that strangers can read if a code will do.

name: Read a contents page to a page
description: Use a contents page to find one section, then check you are on the page it named.
l1c: Pick one line in the contents.
l2c: Open the page number it gives.
l3c: Say whether the heading matches, or how far off you were.
safety: Use a book you may handle. Do not write in a borrowed book.

name: Keep a quote with its page
description: Copy a short quote and the page number in the same note.
l1c: Copy one short line you need into your note.
l2c: Write the page number beside it.
l3c: Find that page from the note.
safety: Copy only what you need. Do not copy a long passage.

name: Write a margin question
description: Write a question in the margin of your own copy, then try to answer it later.
l1c: Write one question beside the passage on your copy or a note.
l2c: Read on before you answer.
l3c: Later, answer it or write that the passage did not.
safety: Do not write in a book you do not own.

name: Arrange tools in the order you use them
description: Lay out the tools for a small task in the order you will pick them up.
l1c: Write the order of tools before you lay them out.
l2c: Place them in that order.
l3c: Do the task and say where the order failed.
safety: Use hand tools for an ordinary task. Do not include a power tool.

name: Cover a finished part
description: Cover a part you have finished so the next step does not mark it.
l1c: Point to the part that is finished.
l2c: Cover it with paper or cloth you may use.
l3c: Do the next ordinary step and then show the covered part is unmarked.
safety: Do not cover a hot part, a vent, or an exit.
